# Exam
The task is to join some non spatial data to some spatial data and wrangle it.

You need **calculate the average percent of science students (in all) grades per county meeting the required standards and produce a map to show where the Country averages are above or below the State of Washington average.**

**Tip** do not try and pull out the number from the % symbol, you have the **count** of students who expected to test and the count who met standard, so you can calculate the percentage.


## Clean data

```{r}
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)

assessmentData <- read_csv('./week2_data/Report_Card_Assessment_Data_2018-19_School_Year_20241008.csv', 
                           locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
                           na = c("", "NA", "NULL"))

spec(assessmentData)
```

# Data manipulation
1.1 Selecting columns
1.2 Group by county
1.3 new column with average percentage 
1.4 new column with average of State of Washington
1.5 new column with above or below average 

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Selecting columns & drop_na
# filter TestSubject = Science, GradeLevel = "All Grades", StudentGroup = 'All students', OrganizationLevel = 'School'
scienceStudentsCountData <- assessmentData %>%
  dplyr::select(contains("County"),
                contains('TestSubject'),
                contains('GradeLevel'),
                contains('StudentGroup'),
                contains('OrganizationLevel'),
                contains("Count of Students Expected to Test"),
                contains("CountMetStandard")) %>%
  filter(TestSubject       == "Science",
         GradeLevel        == "All Grades",
         StudentGroup      == "All Students") %>%
  drop_na(`Count of Students Expected to Test`, CountMetStandard)

head(scienceStudentsCountData)
# To confirm OrganizationLevel is mixed in
# scienceStudentsCountData %>% count(OrganizationLevel)


# group_by and summarise to show one row per county with the totals
# filter out 'multiple' row as it is the state-level summary row.
countySciTotals <- scienceStudentsCountData  %>%
  filter(County != "Multiple",
         OrganizationLevel == "School") %>%
  group_by(County) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalExpectedToTest = sum(`Count of Students Expected to Test`, na.rm = TRUE),
    TotalMetStandard    = sum(CountMetStandard, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(pct_met = TotalMetStandard / TotalExpectedToTest * 100) # Calculate the percentage

countySciTotals

# filter out 'multiple' row as it is the state-level summary row.
# The "Multiple" row
WashingtonRow <- scienceStudentsCountData %>%
  filter(County == "Multiple",
         OrganizationLevel == 'State') %>%
  summarise(
    County = 'Multiple',
    TotalExpectedToTest = sum(`Count of Students Expected to Test`, na.rm = TRUE),
    TotalMetStandard    = sum(CountMetStandard, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(pct_met = TotalMetStandard / TotalExpectedToTest * 100) # Calculate the percentage
WashingtonRow

```

```{r}
comparison

comparison %>%

    diff_Met      = diff(TotalMetStandard),

  )

# Why there is the diffence?
sci <- assessmentData %>%
  filter(TestSubject == "Science", GradeLevel == "All Grades",
         StudentGroup == "All Students", OrganizationLevel == "School")

# 1. School rows lost to suppression / NA
sci %>% filter(is.na(`Count of Students Expected to Test`) | is.na(CountMetStandard)) %>%
  nrow()

# 2. Students in schools labelled "Multiple"
sci %>% filter(County == "Multiple") %>%
  summarise(expected = sum(`Count of Students Expected to Test`, na.rm = TRUE))
```

# 2. Calculate the Washington average and compare
```{r}
stateAvg <- sum(countySciTotals$TotalMetStandard) / sum(countySciTotals$TotalExpectedToTest) * 100
stateAvg
# WashingtonRow might not be correct because of suppressed small groups.

countySciTotals <- countySciTotals %>%
  mutate(vs_state = if_else(pct_met > stateAvg, "Above state average",
                                                "Below state average"))

countySciTotals
```

# 3. Join to the county boundaries and map
```{r}
library(tmap)
library(tmaptools)
library(sf)

washingtonMap <- st_read("./week2_data/Week 2 Homework boundaries-20261015/Washington_Counties_with_Natural_Shoreline___washsh_area.shp")
names(washingtonMap)   # find the column holding the county name -> 'COUNTY'

# plot it
# qtm(washingtonMap)

names(washingtonMap)

  left_join(countySciTotals, c("county" = "County"))

# simple map
qtm(mapData, 
    fill = "pct_met")

# Map to show whether it is below or above the average
# ggplot(mapData) +
#   geom_sf(aes(fill = vs_state), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
#   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Above state average" = "#2c7bb6",
#                                "Below state average" = "#d7191c"),
#                     na.value = "grey80") +
#   labs(title = "Science: % of students meeting standard, 2018–19",
#        subtitle = paste0("Compared with the Washington average of ",
#                          round(stateAvg, 1), "%"),
#        fill = NULL) +
#   theme_void()


# Map shows the gap in percentage points
# Create a column with the difference from the state average, then fill the map with a diverging colour scale centred on zero:
mapData <- mapData %>%
  mutate(diff_from_state = pct_met - stateAvg)

# Make the scale symmetric so equal distances above/below get equal colour strength
maxDiff <- max(abs(mapData$diff_from_state), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(mapData) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = diff_from_state), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#d7191c", mid = "#f7f7f7", high = "#2c7bb6", # Above blue, below red
                       midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-maxDiff, maxDiff),
                       labels = function(x) paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""), x, " pts"),
                       na.value = "grey80",
                       name = "Difference from\nstate average") +
  labs(title = "Science: % of students meeting standard by county, 2018–19",
       subtitle = paste0("Washington average: ", round(stateAvg, 1), "%")) +
  theme_void()

```
